summary: Asks IANA to mark BGP path attribute values 30, 31, 129, 241, 242 and 243 as Deprecated.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8093 asks IANA to mark six BGP path attribute values as deprecated because implementations had used them without assignment. The RFC defines this status as meaning that use is not recommended.

questions: which bgp path attribute values are deprecated
why was bgp attribute value 30 deprecated
what does deprecated mean in the bgp registry
subtitle: Marks six BGP path attribute values as deprecated after unregistered use.

tldr.problem: Some BGP implementations used path attribute values that IANA had not assigned, causing conflicts with later assignments.
tldr.mechanism: IANA marked values 30, 31, 129, 241, 242, and 243 as Deprecated in the BGP Path Attributes subregistry.
tldr.outcome: The Deprecated status means use is not recommended; the RFC says the registry update has no meaningful security consequences.

today: RFC 8093 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Unregistered Attribute Use
sections.content: Some BGP implementations used path attribute values that had not been assigned by IANA. The issue became apparent when IANA initially assigned value 30 to the BGP Large Communities attribute, but an existing implementation used that value for a different data structure. Routes with a valid Large Community attribute were then dropped by that implementation.
sections.plainLanguage: An implementation was already using value 30 when it was assigned to a new attribute. Routes carrying the new attribute were dropped by that implementation.

sections.title: Values Marked Deprecated
sections.content: IANA marked values 30, 31, 129, 241, 242, and 243 as Deprecated in the BGP Path Attributes subregistry. The RFC states that the Deprecated marking means use is not recommended. It says use of the listed values had been confirmed by the involved vendors or by source code review.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA marks six values as Deprecated, meaning their use is not recommended. The RFC says their use was confirmed by vendors or source code review.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that no meaningful security consequences arise from this registry update. Its action is to mark the six named BGP path attribute values as Deprecated.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC says this registry update has no meaningful security consequences.
